seoTitle: Duplicate a Sheet in Smartsheet With Save as New
metaDescription: Clone a Smartsheet sheet, including forms, conditional formatting, and automation workflows, using the Save as New feature for reusable templates.
intro: Rebuilding a proven project setup from scratch wastes time you don't have. Smartsheet's Save as New feature lets you clone an entire sheet, including its formatting rules, forms, and automations, so you can launch new projects from a working template instantly.

steps.heading: Open the file options panel
steps.body: Access the spreadsheet properties or file menu from your active workspace to start the duplication process.

steps.heading: Launch Save as New
steps.body: Use the native Save as New feature to cleanly copy the sheet architecture into your chosen destination.

steps.heading: Decide on data retention
steps.body: Choose whether to preserve the underlying row cell data or start with a blank slate.

steps.heading: Confirm assets carry over
steps.body: Check that attachments, comments, sheet summaries, and shared web forms replicated correctly.

steps.heading: Verify formatting and automations
steps.body: Confirm your conditional formatting color scales and automation workflows migrated into the new sheet, then rename it and reset sharing permissions.

faq.question: Does duplicating a sheet copy the automation workflows too?
faq.answer: Yes, Save as New is designed to migrate your conditional formatting rules and backend automation workflows into the new sheet.

faq.question: Can I duplicate a sheet without copying the data?
faq.answer: Yes, Save as New lets you choose whether to preserve the underlying row data or wipe it for a blank template.

faq.question: Will comments and attachments transfer over?
faq.answer: Yes, the duplication process replicates embedded attachments, row-level comments, and sheet summaries along with the structure.

faq.question: Should I reset sharing permissions on the new sheet?
faq.answer: Yes, it's good practice to rename the duplicated sheet and reset sharing permissions to avoid unintended access.
